title: FX route table (fx: routes/v1)
description: Which `model@provider` serves a capability, what it costs, the features it supports, how many input pictures it takes, its pacing, and the contract that enters its fingerprint (identity.md §7). Tables combine in the order identity.md §7 gives: a later table's entry for the same capability and route replaces an earlier one. An entry may extend another route and state only what differs.

route.description: `<model>@<provider>`, split at the last `@`. A table declares a route at most once per capability.

extends.description: Another route of the same capability and provider, `<model>@<provider>`, that this entry starts from (identity.md §7): an entry already read, else the built-in table's, even when a `--routes` file leaves that table out. The entry takes the base's price, features, input-picture limit, pacing and contract; a member it states replaces the base's, except `contract`, whose members merge one level deep. With it, `price` may be left out. It is not part of the fingerprint.

price.description: What one call costs, low to high: per call, per second, or per thousand characters; or, for a route with no known price, a per-call cap (`cap_usd`). Amounts are US dollars with at most 6 decimal places (identity.md §12). A price states an amount (`usd`, `low_usd`, `high_usd` or `cap_usd`), `0 <= low_usd <= high_usd`, and every tier lies within that range; a reader refuses a table that breaks any of these rules.

cap_usd.description: A capped route: its price is not known, so each call holds this amount and is charged what the provider reports, else the whole cap (adapters.md §5). A call is priced at 0 to the cap. The cap is what FX holds, not a limit the provider honours: a reported cost above it is charged in full. It stands alone.

usd.description: Shorthand for `low_usd` and `high_usd` both set to this amount.

unit.description: What the amounts are per. A call's length is its `text` (characters) or its `max_chars`; or its `duration` (seconds), or `duration_s`.

max_units.description: For a length-priced route: the most units one call can carry, its worst case.

by.description: The request setting whose text value picks a tier, such as `resolution` or `size`. A call whose setting is absent, is not text, is not known to the plan yet, or names no tier is priced at the whole range.

tiers.description: A range per value of `by`, in the price's unit.

allOf.description: A length-priced route declares the most units one call carries.

features.description: What the route supports (`image_input`, `mask`, `alpha`, ...). A step that `requires` another is refused while planning.

max_input_pictures.description: The most input pictures one call takes (`image` and `references`; a mask does not count). A step whose request would carry more is refused while planning (capabilities.md §1).

concurrency.description: The most calls of this route at once.

contract.description: Settings that change what the route returns. Part of its fingerprint, so of every identity it serves. Where an adapter serves the route's capability and provider (one of FX's, one of the family the planning project declares the provider with, or the project adapter it declares it with), a left-out or null `adapter` or `adapter_behavior` is filled in before the fingerprint is taken: from providers.md §2, or with the project adapter's `<path>#<attribute>` and its version or `source:<digest>` (adapters.md §9; identity.md §7).

provider_options.description: Parameters FX does not expose, by provider: the route's provider's adapter adds its member's parameters to what it sends, under a step's own `provider_options` (adapters.md §8). Never a credential.
